name: Molecular and Cellular Biosciences (MCB) PhD Track
detailsNote: Official information available; the December 6 deadline is published without a year and is not confirmed for Fall 2027. Stipend amounts and whether funding covers international students are not stated on the pages checked.
summary: A shared admissions track at Wake Forest School of Medicine for six molecular and cellular PhD programs, with a common first-year curriculum and three lab rotations before choosing a program.

publishedDeadlines.label: Published MCB PhD Track deadline (Fall)
publishedDeadlines.note: Listed in the School of Medicine deadline table without a year or time, and the page says deadlines are subject to change. Not confirmed for Fall 2027; confirm with the program.

timeline.interviews: Most biomedical graduate programs invite selected applicants to interview; the pages do not give MCB-specific interview dates.

english.note: Minimum scores for non-U.S. applicants whose native language is not English.

applicationFee.note: The page says most programs have a $70 fee or a waiver code. Waivers are based on financial need and program participation, and international students are held to the same criteria as domestic students.

requirements.note: Standardized test scores and a CV or resume are listed as optional. Applications not complete 5 business days after the close date are not reviewed.

funding.note: PhD applicants are automatically considered for a full tuition scholarship and stipend for living expenses; no amount is stated. The page does not say whether this covers international students.

international.note: All domestic and international students complete the same online application.
